title: Configurable Capacity Credits & SLA Bundles for Dedicated GPUs
creator: Liam Carter
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers require predictable monthly committed GPU costs but also need headroom for bursty traffic spikes and the ability to scale with seasonal demand. Current reserved capacity packaging options are rigid (monthly committed GPUs + manual burst requests) and create friction for sales and engineering when negotiating contracts or provisioning short-term capacity.

Goal: Design and pilot a set of pricing and packaging primitives that can be assembled into customer-facing SKUs: (1) Capacity Credits (time-boxed GPU-hours or burst credits), (2) Elastic Slabs (auto-scaling pools with guaranteed baseline + capped burst), and (3) SLA Bundles (latency/uptime tiers tied to capacity and failover rules). The strategy should reduce friction in sales, preserve margin by reducing unbounded burst costs, and provide clear upgrade paths from Hosted -> Dedicated.

Scope: Product definition, example price ladders, billing semantics (proration, rollover, transferability), SLA language for contracts, sales playbook, pilot with 2-3 existing enterprise customers, and a small runway engineering scope to make billing and telemetry changes. Legal/Compliance to review updated SQ responses where burst/transferable credits intersect auditability and data residency controls.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 capacity-credit primitives with example pricing and 2 customer-facing SKU compositions
Billing prototype that shows correct proration and consumption accounting for capacity credits in a sandbox billing run
Sales playbook including negotiation guardrails, example contract language for credit exhaustion and replenishment
Legal sign-off on updated security questionnaire entries that reference burst/transfer credits and audit logs
Pilot customers (>=2) contracted under new SKU and telemetry shows <10% SLA breaches attributable to capacity misconfig
Launch checklist for GA including docs, console UI copy, and billing reconciler tickets
metrics: Average monthly revenue per committed GPU increases by >=8% for pilot customers
Burst utilization: percentage of consumed burst credits per month
SLA breach incidents attributable to capacity misconfiguration <= 1 per quarter during pilot
Sales cycle delta: negotiation time reduced by 20% for deals using capacity credits
risks: Uncapped burst consumption could blow margins if credits are mispriced
Engineering complexity: billing reconciliation and token-level telemetry changes required
Legal/regulatory pushback on transferable credits in certain jurisdictions (data residency, audit trails)
Sales misuse: customers expecting unlimited burst without appropriate pricing guardrails
UI/UX confusion in Console leading to incorrect SKU selection or renewal surprises
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: favor deterministic credit units (GPU-hour credits) over opaque 'token' systems to simplify billing and audits
Trade-off: Allow limited rollover of unused credits (max 25%) to increase customer friendliness at cost of marginal revenue deferral
Decision: SLA Bundles will be tiered (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with explicit latency percentiles and availability SLOs tied to guaranteed baseline vs burst capacity
Trade-off: Keep initial burst multiplier conservative (1.5x baseline) to mitigate margin risk, revisit after pilot telemetry
Decision: Transferability of credits between accounts allowed only within same legal entity; cross-entity transfers require special approvals
implementation_notes: Billing: add 'credit bucket' records to billing ledger with start/end and consumed units; prototype in billing-sandbox repo
Telemetry: emit per-request capacity_source tag (baseline|burst|credit) to match consumption against credits
Console: new SKU selector mockups in Figma under /design/dedicated-capacity/credit-skus v2
Engineering scope: minimal runtime gating to prefer baseline pool; allow overflow into burst pool subject to credit availability
Legal: draft standard contract addendum (credit exhaustion and top-up flow) for enterprise agreements
